items.label: Shirley Jackson
items.text: In the manner of Shirley Jackson: small domestic details that slowly turn wrong, told in a calm and reasonable voice.

items.label: P. G. Wodehouse
items.text: In the manner of P. G. Wodehouse: elaborate comic similes, a cheerful narrator and people talking themselves into trouble.

items.label: Raymond Chandler
items.text: In the manner of Raymond Chandler: first-person wisecracks under hard city light, with sharp similes and tired honesty.

items.label: Jane Austen
items.text: In the manner of Jane Austen: dry irony about manners and money, with the narrator's judgment tucked inside polite sentences.

items.label: Ernest Hemingway
items.text: In the manner of Ernest Hemingway: short declarative sentences, concrete nouns, and feeling left under the surface.

items.label: Virginia Woolf
items.text: In the manner of Virginia Woolf: thought moving from one mind to the next, long sentences that follow attention.

items.label: Cormac McCarthy
items.text: In the manner of Cormac McCarthy: long rolling sentences joined by "and", plain speech without quotation marks, a hard landscape.

items.label: Terry Pratchett
items.text: In the manner of Terry Pratchett: warm satire, footnote-style asides worked into the prose, and jokes that turn out to be about people.

items.label: Ursula K. Le Guin
items.text: In the manner of Ursula K. Le Guin: calm, exact prose, a world described through its customs, and choices with weight.

items.label: Agatha Christie
items.text: In the manner of Agatha Christie: brisk scenes, clues placed in plain sight, and characters sketched by one telling habit.

items.label: Elmore Leonard
items.text: In the manner of Elmore Leonard: the story carried by dialogue, loose and funny, with the narration staying out of the way.

items.label: Charles Dickens
items.text: In the manner of Charles Dickens: vivid eccentrics, lists that run on for comic effect, and a narrator who takes sides.

items.label: Kazuo Ishiguro
items.text: In the manner of Kazuo Ishiguro: a restrained narrator who reveals more than they mean to, gently and too late.

items.label: Neil Gaiman
items.text: In the manner of Neil Gaiman: a fairy-tale cadence, ordinary places with a door to somewhere strange, a light touch on dread.

items.label: Toni Morrison
items.text: In the manner of Toni Morrison: rich, rhythmic prose, memory pressing on the present, and names that carry history.

items.label: Douglas Adams
items.text: In the manner of Douglas Adams: deadpan cosmic absurdity, long sentences that end on a joke, and bureaucracy as comedy.

items.label: Anne Rice
items.text: In the manner of Anne Rice: lush sensual description, a confessing narrator, and old houses full of feeling.

items.label: Stephen King
items.text: In the manner of Stephen King: a chatty, close voice, brand names and small-town detail, and fear growing out of the everyday.

items.label: Hilary Mantel
items.text: In the manner of Hilary Mantel: close present tense inside one shrewd mind, history felt as gossip and danger.

items.label: Haruki Murakami
items.text: In the manner of Haruki Murakami: a detached first-person voice, ordinary routines, and strange events accepted calmly.

items.label: Donna Tartt
items.text: In the manner of Donna Tartt: a looking-back narrator, lush detail of rooms and drink, and guilt that colours everything.

items.label: Mark Twain
items.text: In the manner of Mark Twain: a vernacular voice, tall-tale exaggeration, and satire aimed at the respectable.

items.label: Patricia Highsmith
items.text: In the manner of Patricia Highsmith: close to a clever, amoral mind, with everyday details made uneasy.

items.label: Dashiell Hammett
items.text: In the manner of Dashiell Hammett: hard, flat narration of what people do and say, with motives left for the reader.

items.label: Leigh Bardugo
items.text: In the manner of Leigh Bardugo: quick, witty ensemble scenes, schemes within schemes, and wounded people who joke.

items.label: George R. R. Martin
items.text: In the manner of George R. R. Martin: one point-of-view character at a time, politics and appetite, and food described in detail.

items.label: Diana Wynne Jones
items.text: In the manner of Diana Wynne Jones: brisk, funny magic, bickering families, and plots that fold back on themselves.

items.label: Oscar Wilde
items.text: In the manner of Oscar Wilde: epigrams in conversation, elegant surfaces, and moral rot treated as a joke.

items.label: Rainbow Rowell
items.text: In the manner of Rainbow Rowell: warm, funny, specific detail of ordinary life and feelings said out loud with care.

items.label: Sarah Waters
items.text: In the manner of Sarah Waters: careful period detail, slow-building desire, and a twist that rereads what came before.
